content:
maya: quick RFC follow-up — proposal to move 'bench telemetry extraction' out of the intake adapter and into a dedicated bench worker service. idea is: keep intake fast (fingerprint + lightweight smoke) and run heavy microbench/telemetry async. looking for tradeoffs and owners.

maya: key constraints: 1) we must detect gross regressions before serving; 2) intake latency < 200ms p95; 3) reproducible golden-sample measurements; 4) simple rollout path.

dan: +1 on reducing intake latency. question: how do we ensure we still "block" obviously broken models early? if heavy bench is async, we lose that gate. :thinking:

lee: suggestion: split responsibilities. intake = admission gate (fingerprint, signature, quick smoke vector). bench-worker = deep perf/quality signals. if intake smoke fails -> reject. if bench-worker finds regression -> mark model QA-fail and auto-schedule rollback or quarantine.

sofia: important: who owns golden inputs and sampling? if bench-worker reads a central golden manifest, we need RBAC and versioned manifests. also telemetry needs consistent trace ids so ops can stitch intake->bench results.

maya: agreed. proposing a small handshake contract between intake and bench-worker: minimal metadata so bench-worker can fetch exact artifacts and reproduce samples.

maya: example contract (very small):
```json
{
  "model_id": "string",
  "model_fingerprint": "sha256",
  "golden_manifest_uri": "s3://.../manifests/v{n}.json",
  "preferred_samples": ["golden_set_v3"],
  "smoke_status": "pass|fail",
  "admit_ts": "iso8601",
  "trace_id": "uuid"
}
```

dan: that looks fine. couple of concerns: 1) duplication — bench-worker may need a full copy of weights for reproducible microbench; 2) storage/egress costs if we move copies around.

lee: we can avoid full duplication by using immutable URIs and a small local cache on bench instances. bench-worker reads weights by URI, caches by fingerprint. eviction TTL tuned to bench traffic. avoids full duplication on ingest path.

sofia: also add fields for quantization/profile hint (e.g., q4_0, int8) so bench-worker runs the correct binary path. and include expected latency/cost buckets so we can auto-prioritize benches.

maya: good point. updated minimal contract add-ons: "binary_profile": "q4_0", "expected_tail_latency_ms": "number". keep optional.

dan: rollout concerns: how do we transition existing models? we should run bench-worker in shadow mode for 2 weeks (compute-only) and compare signals to current admit decisions. if agreement > 99% then flip canary.

lee: operational ops: need backpressure hooks. bench-worker must not overload storage; include a rate_limit hint in contract and a priority/policy tag.

sofia: monitoring reqs: per-model bench diffs, per-sample variance, and a "regression_score" metric. add alerting thresholds and a manual QA triage link in bench results.

ingest-bot: deploy-bot: bench-worker shadow run scheduled on staging cluster from 2026-04-01 -> 2026-04-15. no traffic routing changes.

maya: action items I can own: 1) draft final handshake spec (contract + error codes) by EOW; 2) add golden-manifest versioning doc; 3) create canary run checklist (shadow metrics to capture).

dan: I'll prototype cache policy and estimate egress costs this week.

lee: I'll sketch bench-worker API (pull contract endpoint + async result webhook). simple endpoints: POST /bench/request -> 202, then POST /bench/result (signed). keep auth via service tokens.

sofia: I'll wire monitoring + trace tags, and draft RBAC requirements for manifest edits.

maya: next check-in Thurs 11am to review handshake draft. any blockers?

dan: none from infra side.

lee: none.

sofia: ok. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — short thread but good alignment.
